review: independent narrow review of offlinePartCoverage eligibility proof
method: Recorded 20 novel intent-fact oracles before inspecting helper source. Each returned result is compared as a whole plan: ordered parts, region, color hex and finish; unsupported/mixed requests must return null. After the oracle was frozen, separately added the two parent-supplied counterexamples plus exact-plan controls. No dispatcher integration, native app, provider or mirror was used.

findings.case: Do not make the hood red.
findings.actual: Returns complete=true with a red hood zone (#c8102e, base::gloss).
findings.expected: Return null because the only requested action is explicitly negated.
findings.evidence: The public offlinePart parser independently returns the same red-hood plan. The coverage residual allow-list consumes 'do not' without checking negation polarity.
findings.risk: If used as an offline-first eligibility gate, the helper can reverse a clear user instruction and apply the prohibited edit.

findings.case: Make the hood red, leave all other panels alone and make the roof blue.
findings.actual: Returns complete=true with only a red hood zone; the roof-blue instruction is absent.
findings.expected: Either return a complete two-zone plan (hood red and roof blue, both gloss) or return null.
findings.evidence: The preservation-clause regex consumes from 'leave all other panels alone' through the end of the sentence, including the later roof instruction.
findings.risk: A configured gate would silently drop a requested change while claiming its plan is complete.

findings.case: Same-color repeated targets and both-sides scope are rejected by the coverage wrapper.
findings.actual: offlinePartCoverage returns null for 'Make the hood and roof both red, with all other panels unchanged.' and 'Make both sides red.' The exported offlinePart function builds exact complete two-zone plans for both.
findings.expected: The wrapper may safely prove these plans if all part/color/finish associations are retained.
findings.risk: Safe, representable requests cannot use this coverage route.

integration_review.dispatcher: No production dispatcher integration was present in this source snapshot; this report makes no claim about runtime routing.
integration_review.api_shape: offlinePartCoverage returns kind, zones, parts, finish and complete. It does not return canonicalText, source spans, explicit-finish metadata, or preservation/scope evidence. The structured zones are the only normalized plan available to a caller.
integration_review.color_only_finish: A color-only request such as 'Make my hood blue, please.' is accepted with finish base::gloss. The API does not mark gloss as an inferred default. A consumer must prefer the existing exact-part/color-only path that preserves current finish, or carry explicit-finish provenance, before using this candidate plan.
integration_review.safe_routing_boundary: Do not route the original utterance merely because complete is true; both P1 examples demonstrate that complete can describe a lossy or polarity-reversed plan. A future caller should apply a validated structured plan or consume an independently verified canonical representation only after the false-positive cases are fixed.

limitations: The 20 pre-inspection cases focus on mixed scope, direction, unsupported parts/finish/color descriptors, negation and preservation language; most are intended to fail closed under the helper's deliberately narrow contract.
The existing producer contract/report was read for context but not modified. This reviewer did not run it because it writes the producer-owned report artifact.
The current source was stable at the recorded hash during the review.
